title: Typed source and tail data for tensor representative normalization
statement: For Q:C→D and R:K→C, with C,D monoidal, and QB:L→D, record an actual tensor operation t:K→K→K, a predicate S closed under t, an object function W:K→L, source factors RX tensor RY→R(t(X,Y)), Q(RX)→QB(W(X)), W(t(X,Y))→Z(X,Y), and a tail Q(RX) tensor Q(RY)→QB(Z(X,Y)). Neither K nor L needs a monoidal structure in the interface. Define the common target as QB(Z(X,Y)) and the source as Q(first) followed by second evaluated at t(X,Y) and QB(third). Also record proofs that the first factor is invertible on S-pairs, the single-input second factor is invertible on S, and the third is always invertible. All object and map data are actual separately supplied constructions; proof fields supply no data. Its Normalized(d,h) predicate is the complete equation for all pairs satisfying S, namely d.source(X,Y) = inverse(h.muIso(RX,RY)) followed by d.tail(X,Y). The predicate is formed in the abstract categories before concrete scalar specialization.

proof.text: Form the structure with the representative tensor operation, its predicate-closure proof, single-input second comparison, source factors, target and tail. Define obj and source by the actual target and abstract three-factor composite. Invertibility certificates are proof fields. Keeping the single-input comparison and its property before evaluation at t(X,Y) avoids expanding a concrete cochain tensor inside its certificate.

proof_origin: J2, 2026-10-26: a definition/API repair for the slow concrete cochain normalization. The actual diagram is constructed in a typed record; its K-flat source property is proved from existing APIs. This does not split a proof to evade the file limit. The complete normalization predicate is also formed generically. This avoids repeating concrete cochain monoidal instance conversions in the finite-level uniqueness application. The common-target method obj is a reducible abbreviation of QB.obj(target), so the source and tail have the same target already under the rewriting tactics' implicit transparency.
